title: PRD: MCPack v1.1
summary: v1.1 milestone PRD adding semantic search via optional EmbeddingProvider hook and tool-usage analytics via getAnalytics(), preserving all v1.0 invariants.
scope_summary: MCPack v1.1 (Search & Observability) introduces two additive capabilities: (1) optional semantic search via a minimal EmbeddingProvider interface with hybrid keyword+semantic ranking, plus a separate @llvs/mcpack-embeddings adapter package for local MiniLM; and (2) in-memory, role-scoped tool-usage analytics surfaced via a getAnalytics() method on the server handle. Both features are strictly additive — public API signatures remain byte-for-byte identical, the core package adds zero new runtime dependencies, ESM-only output is preserved, opaque denial semantics are maintained, and v1.0 keyword-only behavior is the exact fallback when no embeddings are configured.
locked_decisions: Public API (mcpack(), createMCPackServer() signatures) is byte-for-byte identical to v1.0 — zero breaking changes
@llvs/mcpack core package adds zero new runtime dependencies in v1.1
v1.1 remains ESM-only with NodeNext module resolution, TypeScript strict + verbatimModuleSyntax — no CommonJS output
MCPack core ships no embedding implementation — EmbeddingProvider is a user-supplied hook
@xenova/transformers and any model dependencies live exclusively in @llvs/mcpack-embeddings, never in core
google-auth-library and any auth dependencies live in resolver packages, never in core
Role filtering is applied after ranking, not before — preserves opaque denial invariant
Out-of-role tools/call still returns 'Unknown tool: {name}' — opaque denial preserved
tools/list always returns exactly one tool (search_tools) with no v1.1-added latency
Schemas loaded once per session still return as {loaded: true} references — session invariant preserved
All analytics data is in-memory only — no disk writes, no network egress, resets on process restart
Analytics for a given role must never expose the existence of tools outside that role
getAnalytics() is on the server handle, not exposed as an MCP tool — never callable by agents
Stripe MCP harness must show at least 80.7% aggregate token reduction with hybrid ranking — no regression vs v1.0
When no EmbeddingProvider is configured, search path is identical to v1.0 at the code level — no performance regression
Test count must reach at least 120 with at least 99% statement coverage
success_criteria: Test count is at least 120 with at least 99% statement coverage
Stripe MCP harness shows at least 80.7% aggregate token reduction with hybrid ranking enabled (no regression vs v1.0)
Semantic search recall improves at least 15% on the held-out 50-query intent benchmark vs v1.0 keyword baseline when MiniLM adapter is configured
search_tools p99 latency with local MiniLM adapter is at most 50ms above v1.0 baseline on commodity hardware
Semantic index build completes within 5 seconds for a 50-tool server using local MiniLM adapter
mcpack() and createMCPackServer() signatures are byte-for-byte identical to v1.0
@llvs/mcpack package.json lists zero new runtime dependencies
getAnalytics() returns accurate event counts matching a known call sequence in integration tests
Analytics for a given role contain zero references to tools outside that role
getAnalytics() is not callable via any MCP tool — verified by integration test attempting to call it as an agent
non_goals: Persistent session storage — v1.1 stays fully in-memory (v2.0)
Standalone proxy server process — MCPack remains a library (v2.0)
OTEL exporter or structured log output for analytics (v1.2)
Webhook or callback hook for analytics events (v1.2)
Multi-source / multi-MCP gateway mode (tracked separately in multi-source PRD)
Google OAuth or any auth resolver (tracked separately in partner hub PRD)
HTTP/SSE transport (tracked separately in partner hub PRD)
Shipping a default embedding model inside @llvs/mcpack core
open_questions: Should getAnalytics() be on the server handle returned by mcpack() / createMCPackServer(), or on a separate analytics property of that handle? Separate property is cleaner for tree-shaking; flat handle is simpler.
Should hybrid ranking weights be configurable per-query or only at config time? Per-query is more flexible but adds API surface.

Should the semantic index be rebuilt if the upstream server's tool list changes at runtime (via listChanged notification)? v1.0 builds the keyword index once at startup — semantic could follow the same pattern and defer dynamic rebuild to v1.2.
What is the target benchmark for the 50-query intent recall test — built from Stripe MCP, a generic synthetic set, or contributed by the community?

Should denial events in analytics record the denied tool name at all, even for operators? Operator queries with no role filter would see all denial events including tool names — intentional for debugging but should be explicitly decided.
Should @llvs/mcpack-embeddings ship a hosted API adapter (OpenAI, Voyage) in addition to the local MiniLM adapter for v1.1, or defer all hosted adapters to v1.2?

risks.risk: @xenova/transformers + MiniLM model weight adds significant install size to @llvs/mcpack-embeddings
risks.impact: Medium — operators installing the adapter package see a large download
risks.mitigation: Keep adapter in separate package so core users are unaffected. Document model size clearly in adapter README.

risks.risk: Embedding query latency exceeds 50ms budget on low-powered Railway instances
risks.mitigation: Benchmark on Railway free tier before GA. If latency exceeds budget, cache query embeddings for repeated identical queries within a session.

risks.risk: Semantic search quality regresses keyword baseline on tool surfaces with very short or cryptic names
risks.impact: Medium — hybrid ranking helps but short names have poor embedding signal
risks.mitigation: Hybrid ranking with 0.7/0.3 default weights preserves keyword floor. Operators can tune weights toward keyword-heavy if needed.

risks.risk: Analytics memory growth unbounded in long-running sessions with high call volume
risks.impact: Low for typical use, Medium for high-throughput production
risks.mitigation: Cap event arrays at a configurable maxEvents (default 10,000). Oldest events dropped when cap is reached.

risks.risk: MCP SDK internal _requestHandlers Map (used by wrap mode) changes in a future SDK release
risks.impact: High if it breaks wrap mode entirely
risks.mitigation: Already tracked in v1.0 known risks. v1.1 adds a startup assertion that verifies the handler map is accessible and throws a clear error if not.

risks.risk: Semantic index not ready when first query arrives
risks.mitigation: Fall back to keyword scoring for queries that arrive before index is ready. Log a warning. Never block search_tools response.
